blocks.content: We don't have to choose one or the other. We can use both:

items: Keep an outer <Suspense> as a safety net.
Add inner boundaries for specific routes.

blocks.content: React always uses the nearest ancestor, so the inner one wins when both are present. If a route doesn't have its own boundary, the outer one catches it.
Both patterns are valid. The tradeoff is effort vs. polish:

items: One outer boundary is quick to set up and works well for prototypes.
Per-route boundaries take a bit more wiring, but the user gets a tailored loading experience for each page.

blocks.content: We can start with one and move to the other as the app grows. Now let's build a real skeleton loader we can use as a fallback.
